title: Domoda au Poisson, Sauce Béchamel Sénégalaise
author: Chef Bineta Diallo Dioh (Slow Food Foundation for Biodiversity with FAO)
desc: Fried fish soaked two minutes in a tomato sauce built from oil, tomato paste, cherry tomatoes and a litre of water, enriched with dried fish and yeet and thickened with flour diluted in half a glass of water — a Senegalese ‘béchamel’ made without milk.
longDesc: The Slow Food and FAO booklet ‘Sénégal: de la terre à la table’ credits this recipe to chef Bineta Diallo Dioh and writes it for 10 people. Ten medium fish are fried; tomato paste and crushed cherry tomatoes are cooked a minute in 250 ml of oil; a litre of water goes in with vegetables of choice, dried fish and yeet; when the vegetables are cooked the fried fish go in to soak for two minutes; and the sauce is thickened with 30 g of wheat flour diluted in half a glass of water. It is served over white rice, which the booklet names niangkatang. THE RESEARCH NOTES CAPTURED THE FIGURES AND THE CUES ABOVE BUT NOT THE STEP-BY-STEP ORDER: where the onion, garlic, vinegar or lemon, dried fish and yeet enter the pot, and how the fish is fried, is not recorded here. Check the original booklet before cooking.
ingredients: 1 spoonful vinegar or lemon juice, to your taste
Vegetables of your choice — quantity not printed
25 g yeet (fermented dried sea snail, SEN089)
Salt, pepper and chilli (optional) — quantities not printed
steps: Fry the fish. The method and time for the frying are not recorded in the research notes.
Cook the tomato paste and the crushed cherry tomatoes in the oil for one minute. Where the onion and garlic are cooked in relation to this step is not recorded.
Add the litre of water and the vegetables of your choice, with the dried fish and the yeet. The order and timing of these additions are not recorded.
When the vegetables are cooked, put the fried fish in to soak in the sauce for 2 minutes.
Thicken with the flour diluted in half a glass of water. No temperature is printed.
Serve over white rice (the booklet names it niangkatang).
chefTips: The one quoted cue is that the fried fish go into the sauce only ‘when the vegetables are cooked’.
The booklet makes the sauce for 10 people; scale down with care because the flour and dried fish are small fixed quantities.
Dissolve the flour in the half glass of water before adding it, so it does not clump.
commonMistakes: Cooking the fried fish in the sauce for longer than 2 minutes.
reheating: Reheat gently; the page prints no instructions.
healthBenefits: The sauce is vegetable-rich and the fish is the protein.
culturalNote: ‘Béchamel sénégalaise’ is the booklet’s own name for the flour-thickened tomato sauce; it contains no milk or butter. Compare domoda with peanut butter, SEN025.
sources: Source: ‘produits et plats traditionnels / Sénégal / de la terre à la table’, Slow Food Foundation for Biodiversity with FAO (project GTF/RAF/426/ITA), directed by Velia Lucidi and Serena Milano; texts Serena Berisio; recipes credited to chef Bineta Diallo Dioh; translation and edition Pierre Le Chevallier. Date: none printed (2010 appears only for the Mille Jardins launch). Yield ‘Pour 10 personnes’. TWO-PASS, line-level agreement at two independent URLs (fao.org and fondazioneslowfood.com), quantities identical.

Quoted cue: ‘Quand les légumes sont cuits, mettre les poissons frits à tremper dans cette sauce pendant 2 minutes’. Method figures captured: one minute for the tomato paste and cherry tomatoes; 1 litre of water; 2 minutes soaking; flour diluted in ‘un demi-verre d’eau’. No temperature printed.

ABSENT, stated in the entry: quantity of vegetables, salt, pepper and chilli; the frying method; and the order of the onion, garlic, vinegar or lemon, dried fish and yeet. Total prep and cook times are NOT printed; the 30 and 35 minutes above are scheduling estimates, not source data.
